question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 9 & 6 & 6 \\ -2 & -6 & -2 & -4 \\ 1 & 6 & -4 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 9 & 6 & 6 \\ -2 & -6 & -2 & -4 \\ 1 & 6 & -4 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & -6 & -2 & -4 \\ 1 & 6 & -4 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 6 & -4 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -6 & -9\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -6 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

metadata.domain: x,y,z real; p,q,s nonzero; nonsingular 3-by-3 coefficient matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -2 & 0 & -10 \\ -1 & -1 & -3 & 7 \\ -2 & -3 & 2 & -11\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -2 & 0 & -10 \\ -1 & -1 & -3 & 7 \\ -2 & -3 & 2 & -11\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ -1 & -1 & -3 & 7 \\ -2 & -3 & 2 & -11\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 12 \\ -2 & -3 & 2 & -11\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 12 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 12\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-1R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 12\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-4 \\ y &=1-(-2)(-4) \\ &=-7 \\ x &=5-(1)(-7) \\ &\quad -(0)(-4) \\ &=12\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(12,-7,-4\right)
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -8\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -8\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=4 \\ y &=0-(1)(4) \\ &=-4 \\ x &=-1-(2)(-4) \\ &\quad -(2)(4) \\ &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-1,-4,4\right)
$$
